extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, grant applicants, research administrators, and small business applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries and updates about NIH grants policies, application formats, review processes, and resources applicants should follow when preparing or managing NIH extramural grant proposals and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer models that are scientifically sound and most appropriate to the research question; NAMs are encouraged for human relevance and translational potential but must be justified as the right choice for the specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan format available. We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for NIH applications, use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format; check the new format for what elements are required and follow it exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in research
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic. The reliability of biomedical research is foundational... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and award activities should include plans and practices that promote replication and reproducibility; expect NIH to highlight and prioritize efforts that demonstrate commitment to these principles and consult the Gold Standard Science plan and related initiative for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects format and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PF5 application format and follow the award-structure guidance (including potential splitting into linked awards after review). Review the PF5 overview materials to ensure compliance with format and structural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand review scoring categories and 'competitive but not discussed'
rubrics_metrics.description: "My Application Was Scored as 'Competitive But Not Discussed' During Review. What Does This Mean? ... the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of NIH review cutoffs: not all scored applications are discussed; a designation of 'competitive but not discussed' reflects placement in the middle third under current procedures. Applicants should understand how these categories affect next steps (e.g., Just-in-Time) and pay attention to any process changes from emergency modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for centralized peer review changes (CSR consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency. In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that peer review processes and administrative handling may have changed due to centralization; check CSR guidance and announcements for how consolidation affects study section assignment, review timelines, and applicant expectations.
